Iff.mpr.code: Iff.mpr {a b : Prop} (self : a ↔ b) : b → a
Iff.mpr.comment: Modus ponens for if and only if, reversed. If `a ↔ b` and `b`, then `a`.
Iff.mpr.description: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.

Exists.intro.code: Exists.intro.{u} {α : Sort u} {p : α → Prop} (w : α) (h : p w) : Exists p
Exists.intro.comment:
Existential introduction. If `a : α` and `h : p a`,
then `⟨a, h⟩` is a proof that `∃ x : α, p x`.
Exists.intro.description: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.

Iff.mp.code: Iff.mp {a b : Prop} (self : a ↔ b) : a → b
Iff.mp.comment: Modus ponens for if and only if. If `a ↔ b` and `a`, then `b`.
Iff.mp.description: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.

HasSubset.Subset.code: HasSubset.Subset.{u} {α : Type u} [self : HasSubset α] : α → α → Prop
HasSubset.Subset.description: The subset relation describes the condition under which one set is contained within another.

Iff.trans.code: Iff.trans {a b c : Prop} (h₁ : a ↔ b) (h₂ : b ↔ c) : a ↔ c
Iff.trans.description: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.

PSum.inl.code: PSum.inl.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} (val : α) : α ⊕' β
PSum.inl.comment: Left injection into the sum type `α ⊕' β`. If `a : α` then `.inl a : α ⊕' β`.
PSum.inl.description: Injecting an element from one type into a sum type consists of representing that element as belonging to the first component of the sum.

PSum.inr.code: PSum.inr.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} (val : β) : α ⊕' β
PSum.inr.comment: Right injection into the sum type `α ⊕' β`. If `b : β` then `.inr b : α ⊕' β`.
PSum.inr.description: The right injection into a sum type allows any element from one set to be represented as an element of the combined set.

Sigma.mk.sizeOf_spec.code:
Sigma.mk.sizeOf_spec.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : α → Type v} [SizeOf α] [(a : α) → SizeOf (β a)] (fst : α) (snd : β fst) :
  sizeOf ⟨fst, snd⟩ = 1 + sizeOf fst + sizeOf snd
Sigma.mk.sizeOf_spec.description: The size of a dependent pair is equal to one plus the sizes of its individual components.

Iff.rfl.description: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.

Quotient.code: Quotient.{u} {α : Sort u} (s : Setoid α) : Sort u
Quotient.comment:
`Quotient α s` is the same as `Quot α r`, but it is specialized to a setoid `s`
(that is, an equivalence relation) instead of an arbitrary relation.
Prefer `Quotient` over `Quot` if your relation is actually an equivalence relation.
Quotient.fullDefinition: def Quotient {α : Sort u} (s : Setoid α) :=   @Quot α Setoid.r
Quotient.description: The quotient of a set using an equivalence relation is a type that represents the distinct equivalence classes formed by that relation.

Ne.symm.code: Ne.symm.{u} {α : Sort u} {a b : α} (h : a ≠ b) : b ≠ a
Ne.symm.description: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.

Sum.inl.code: Sum.inl.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (val : α) : α ⊕ β
Sum.inl.comment: Left injection into the sum type `α ⊕ β`. If `a : α` then `.inl a : α ⊕ β`.
Sum.inl.description: The left injection function constructs a sum type from an element of the first type.

Sum.inr.code: Sum.inr.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (val : β) : α ⊕ β
Sum.inr.comment: Right injection into the sum type `α ⊕ β`. If `b : β` then `.inr b : α ⊕ β`.
Sum.inr.description: The right injection into the sum type combines an element from one type with the sum type, indicating it originates from the second type.

funext.code: funext.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {β : α → Sort v} {f g : (x : α) → β x} (h : ∀ (x : α), f x = g x) : f = g
funext.comment:
**Function extensionality** is the statement that if two functions take equal values
every point, then the functions themselves are equal: `(∀ x, f x = g x) → f = g`.
It is called "extensionality" because it talks about how to prove two objects are equal
based on the properties of the object (compare with set extensionality,
which is `(∀ x, x ∈ s ↔ x ∈ t) → s = t`).

This is often an axiom in dependent type theory systems, because it cannot be proved
from the core logic alone. However in lean's type theory this follows from the existence
of quotient types (note the `Quot.sound` in the proof, as well as the `show` line
which makes use of the definitional equality `Quot.lift f h (Quot.mk x) = f x`).
funext.description: If two functions yield the same output for every input, then those functions are considered equal.

Iff.intro.code: Iff.intro {a b : Prop} (mp : a → b) (mpr : b → a) : a ↔ b
Iff.intro.comment: If `a → b` and `b → a` then `a` and `b` are equivalent.
Iff.intro.description: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.

Singleton.singleton.code: Singleton.singleton.{u, v} {α : outParam (Type u)} {β : Type v} [self : Singleton α β] : α → β
Singleton.singleton.comment: `singleton x` is a collection with the single element `x` (notation: `{x}`).
Singleton.singleton.description: A singleton is a collection that contains exactly one element.

Iff.symm.code: Iff.symm {a b : Prop} (h : a ↔ b) : b ↔ a
Iff.symm.description: If two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.

Sigma.mk.code: Sigma.mk.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : α → Type v} (fst : α) (snd : β fst) : Sigma β
Sigma.mk.comment:
Constructor for a dependent pair. If `a : α` and `b : β a` then `⟨a, b⟩ : Sigma β`.
(This will usually require a type ascription to determine `β`
since it is not determined from `a` and `b` alone.)
Sigma.mk.description: A dependent pair is constructed from an element and a corresponding value that depends on that element, encapsulated together in a specific type.

Union.union.code: Union.union.{u} {α : Type u} [self : Union α] : α → α → α
Union.union.comment: `a ∪ b` is the union of`a` and `b`.
Union.union.description: The union of two elements is defined as the combination of both elements into a single entity.

Ne.code: Ne.{u} {α : Sort u} (a b : α) : Prop
Ne.comment:
`a ≠ b`, or `Ne a b` is defined as `¬ (a = b)` or `a = b → False`,
and asserts that `a` and `b` are not equal.
Ne.fullDefinition: @[reducible] def Ne {α : Sort u} (a b : α) :=   ¬(a = b)
Ne.description: The inequality between two elements is defined by the negation of their equality, asserting that they are distinct.

Sigma.fst.code: Sigma.fst.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : α → Type v} (self : Sigma β) : α
Sigma.fst.comment: The first component of a dependent pair. If `p : @Sigma α β` then `p.1 : α`.
Sigma.fst.fullDefinition: fst : α   /-- The second component of a dependent pair. If `p : Sigma β` then `p.2 : β p.1`. -/   snd : β fst
Sigma.fst.description: The first component of a dependent pair is extracted from the pair, returning the value of the first type.

Quot.liftOn.code:
Quot.liftOn.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} {r : α → α → Prop} (q : Quot r) (f : α → β)
  (c : ∀ (a b : α), r a b → f a = f b) : β
Quot.liftOn.comment:
`Quot.liftOn q f h` is the same as `Quot.lift f h q`. It just reorders
the argument `q : Quot r` to be first.
Quot.liftOn.fullDefinition: protected abbrev liftOn {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} {r : α → α → Prop}   (q : Quot r) (f : α → β) (c : (a b : α) → r a b → f a = f b) : β :=   lift f c q
Quot.liftOn.description: The process of lifting a function onto the quotient of a set, while ensuring that equivalent elements map to the same value, can be rearranged so that the quotient appears as the first argument.

Subsingleton.intro.code: Subsingleton.intro.{u} {α : Sort u} (allEq : ∀ (a b : α), a = b) : Subsingleton α
Subsingleton.intro.comment: Construct a proof that `α` is a subsingleton by showing that any two elements are equal.
Subsingleton.intro.description: A type is a subsingleton if it can be shown that all of its elements are equal to each other.

Function.comp_apply.code:
Function.comp_apply.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {β : Sort u_1} {δ : Sort u_2} {α : Sort u_3} {f : β → δ} {g : α → β} {x : α} :
  (f ∘ g) x = f (g x)
Function.comp_apply.description: The composition of two functions applied to an argument is equal to applying the first function to the result of applying the second function to that argument.

Not.imp.description: If a proposition implies another proposition which is false, then the first proposition must also be false.

Or.symm.code: Or.symm {a b : Prop} : a ∨ b → b ∨ a
Or.symm.description: The disjunction operation is symmetric, meaning that if one proposition is true or the other, then the order of these propositions can be reversed.

SDiff.sdiff.code: SDiff.sdiff.{u} {α : Type u} [self : SDiff α] : α → α → α
SDiff.sdiff.comment:
`a \ b` is the set difference of `a` and `b`,
consisting of all elements in `a` that are not in `b`.
SDiff.sdiff.description: The set difference operation identifies all elements in one set that do not belong to another set.

if_pos.code: if_pos.{u} {c : Prop} {h : Decidable c} (hc : c) {α : Sort u} {t e : α} : (if c then t else e) = t
if_pos.description: If a condition is true, then the result of a conditional expression evaluating that condition will equal the first option.

if_neg.code: if_neg.{u} {c : Prop} {h : Decidable c} (hnc : ¬c) {α : Sort u} {t e : α} : (if c then t else e) = e
if_neg.description: If a condition is proven to be false, then the result of a conditional expression will yield the alternative value.

dif_pos.code: dif_pos.{u} {c : Prop} {h : Decidable c} (hc : c) {α : Sort u} {t : c → α} {e : ¬c → α} : dite c t e = t hc
dif_pos.description: The result of a dependent function based on a decidable proposition is equal to the function defined for the true case when that proposition holds.

dif_neg.code: dif_neg.{u} {c : Prop} {h : Decidable c} (hnc : ¬c) {α : Sort u} {t : c → α} {e : ¬c → α} : dite c t e = e hnc
dif_neg.description: If a proposition is false, then the result of a dependent choice between two outcomes based on its truth will be equal to the outcome corresponding to its falsity.

Eq.comm.code: Eq.comm.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {a b : α} : a = b ↔ b = a
Eq.comm.description: Equality is symmetric, meaning if one element equals another, then the second element equals the first.

And.comm.code: And.comm {a b : Prop} : a ∧ b ↔ b ∧ a
And.comm.description: The conjunction of two propositions is commutative, meaning that the order in which they are combined does not affect their truth.

mt.description: If a true implication leads to a false conclusion, then the antecedent must also be false.

eq_self_iff_true.code: eq_self_iff_true.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} (a : α) : a = a ↔ True
eq_self_iff_true.description: The assertion that an element is equal to itself is logically equivalent to stating that a truth exists.

List.cons.injEq.code:
List.cons.injEq.{u} {α : Type u} (head : α) (tail : List α) :
  ∀ (head_1 : α) (tail_1 : List α), (head :: tail = head_1 :: tail_1) = (head = head_1 ∧ tail = tail_1)
List.cons.injEq.description: The equation asserts that two lists constructed with the same head and tail are equal if and only if their heads and tails are individually equal.

Prod.map.code:
Prod.map.{u₁, u₂, v₁, v₂} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {β₁ : Type v₁} {β₂ : Type v₂} (f : α₁ → α₂) (g : β₁ → β₂) :
  α₁ × β₁ → α₂ × β₂
Prod.map.comment:
`Prod.map f g : α₁ × β₁ → α₂ × β₂` maps across a pair
by applying `f` to the first component and `g` to the second.
Prod.map.fullDefinition: def Prod.map {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {β₁ : Type v₁} {β₂ : Type v₂}     (f : α₁ → α₂) (g : β₁ → β₂) : α₁ × β₁ → α₂ × β₂   | (a, b) => (f a, g b)
Prod.map.description: A mapping function transforms a pair of elements by applying one function to the first element and another function to the second element.

Sigma.snd.code: Sigma.snd.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : α → Type v} (self : Sigma β) : β self.fst
Sigma.snd.comment: The second component of a dependent pair. If `p : Sigma β` then `p.2 : β p.1`.
Sigma.snd.description: The second component of a dependent pair extracts the value associated with the first element from the pair.

Nat.add_zero.description: Adding zero to a natural number does not change its value.

flip.code: flip.{u, v, w} {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} {φ : Sort w} (f : α → β → φ) : β → α → φ
flip.comment:
`flip f a b` is `f b a`. It is useful for "point-free" programming,
since it can sometimes be used to avoid introducing variables.
For example, `(·<·)` is the less-than relation,
and `flip (·<·)` is the greater-than relation.
flip.fullDefinition: @[inline] def flip {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} {φ : Sort w} (f : α → β → φ) : β → α → φ :=   fun b a => f a b
flip.description: Reversing the order of the inputs to a function allows the function to accept its second argument first, effectively swapping the positions of the two arguments.

Subtype.eta.code: Subtype.eta.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} (a : { x // p x }) (h : p ↑a) : ⟨↑a, h⟩ = a
Subtype.eta.description: For any element of a subtype, reconstructing that element from its underlying value and proof of property yields equality with the original element.

Subtype.eq.code: Subtype.eq.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {a1 a2 : { x // p x }} : ↑a1 = ↑a2 → a1 = a2
Subtype.eq.description: If two elements of a subtype have the same underlying value, then they are considered equal as elements of that subtype.

Function.comp_def.code:
Function.comp_def.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {δ : Sort u_3} (f : β → δ) (g : α → β) :
  f ∘ g = fun x => f (g x)
Function.comp_def.description: The composition of two functions is defined as a new function that takes an input, applies the second function to it, and then applies the first function to the result.

HasEquiv.Equiv.code: HasEquiv.Equiv.{u, v} {α : Sort u} [self : HasEquiv α] : α → α → Sort v
HasEquiv.Equiv.comment:
`x ≈ y` says that `x` and `y` are equivalent. Because this is a typeclass,
the notion of equivalence is type-dependent.
HasEquiv.Equiv.description: The concept of equivalence between elements is defined in a way that is dependent on the specific type of the elements being compared.

Quotient.mk.code: Quotient.mk.{u} {α : Sort u} (s : Setoid α) (a : α) : Quotient s
Quotient.mk.comment: The canonical quotient map into a `Quotient`.
Quotient.mk.fullDefinition: protected def mk {α : Sort u} (s : Setoid α) (a : α) : Quotient s :=   Quot.mk Setoid.r a
Quotient.mk.description: The canonical quotient map transforms an element into its associated equivalence class under a given setoid.

Quotient.exists_rep.code: Quotient.exists_rep.{u} {α : Sort u} {s : Setoid α} (q : Quotient s) : ∃ a, ⟦a⟧ = q
Quotient.exists_rep.description: For any equivalence class represented by a quotient, there exists a representative element from which the class is constructed.

Quotient.sound.code: Quotient.sound.{u} {α : Sort u} {s : Setoid α} {a b : α} : a ≈ b → ⟦a⟧ = ⟦b⟧
Quotient.sound.comment:
The analogue of `Quot.sound`: If `a` and `b` are related by the equivalence relation,
then they have equal equivalence classes.
Quotient.sound.description: If two elements are related by an equivalence relation, their respective equivalence classes are equal.

Quotient.lift.code:
Quotient.lift.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} {s : Setoid α} (f : α → β) :
  (∀ (a b : α), a ≈ b → f a = f b) → Quotient s → β
Quotient.lift.comment:
The analogue of `Quot.lift`: if `f : α → β` respects the equivalence relation `≈`,
then it lifts to a function on `Quotient s` such that `lift f h (mk a) = f a`.
Quotient.lift.fullDefinition: protected abbrev lift {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} {s : Setoid α} (f : α → β) : ((a b : α) → a ≈ b → f a = f b) → Quotient s → β :=   Quot.lift f
Quotient.lift.description: If a function respects an equivalence relation, it can be uniquely extended to operate on the quotient of the set by that relation.

Quotient.recOn.code:
Quotient.recOn.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {s : Setoid α} {motive : Quotient s → Sort v} (q : Quotient s)
  (f : (a : α) → motive ⟦a⟧) (h : ∀ (a b : α) (p : a ≈ b), ⋯ ▸ f a = f b) : motive q
Quotient.recOn.fullDefinition: protected abbrev recOn     (q : Quotient s)     (f : (a : α) → motive (Quotient.mk s a))     (h : (a b : α) → (p : a ≈ b) → Eq.ndrec (f a) (Quotient.sound p) = f b)     : motive q :=   Quot.recOn q f h
Quotient.recOn.description: This definition describes a method for constructing a type from a quotient of a set given a setoid, a motive for the quotient, and a function that assigns values to representatives of the equivalence classes while ensuring that equivalent elements yield the same result.

PSigma.mk.code: PSigma.mk.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {β : α → Sort v} (fst : α) (snd : β fst) : PSigma β
PSigma.mk.comment:
Constructor for a dependent pair. If `a : α` and `b : β a` then `⟨a, b⟩ : PSigma β`.
(This will usually require a type ascription to determine `β`
since it is not determined from `a` and `b` alone.)
PSigma.mk.description: A dependent pair constructor allows the creation of a pair that associates an element with a type that depends on that element.

Setoid.mk.code: Setoid.mk.{u} {α : Sort u} (r : α → α → Prop) (iseqv : Equivalence r) : Setoid α
Setoid.mk.description: A setoid is defined as a type equipped with an equivalence relation.

Equivalence.mk.code:
Equivalence.mk.{u} {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} (refl : ∀ (x : α), r x x) (symm : ∀ {x y : α}, r x y → r y x)
  (trans : ∀ {x y z : α}, r x y → r y z → r x z) : Equivalence r
Equivalence.mk.description: A relation that is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive defines an equivalence relation.

HasSubset.mk.code: HasSubset.mk.{u} {α : Type u} (Subset : α → α → Prop) : HasSubset α
HasSubset.mk.description: A subset relation can be defined for a type by specifying the properties that determine when one element is considered a subset of another.

EmptyCollection.mk.code: EmptyCollection.mk.{u} {α : Type u} (emptyCollection : α) : EmptyCollection α
EmptyCollection.mk.description: An empty collection is defined as a type with an element that represents no items.

Insert.mk.code: Insert.mk.{u, v} {α : outParam (Type u)} {γ : Type v} (insert : α → γ → γ) : Insert α γ
Insert.mk.description: An insertion operation is defined that allows incorporating elements of one type into a collection of another type.

Singleton.mk.code: Singleton.mk.{u, v} {α : outParam (Type u)} {β : Type v} (singleton : α → β) : Singleton α β
Singleton.mk.description: A singleton type is constructed from a function that maps an element of the first type to the second type.

LawfulSingleton.mk.code:
LawfulSingleton.mk.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [EmptyCollection β] [Insert α β] [Singleton α β]
  (insert_emptyc_eq : ∀ (x : α), insert x ∅ = {x}) : LawfulSingleton α β
LawfulSingleton.mk.description: A lawful singleton structure is established when inserting an element into an empty collection results in a collection containing only that element.

Sep.mk.code: Sep.mk.{u, v} {α : outParam (Type u)} {γ : Type v} (sep : (α → Prop) → γ → γ) : Sep α γ
Sep.mk.description: The construction of a separation operator creates a new type that allows for the extraction of elements from a type based on a predicate.

Union.mk.code: Union.mk.{u} {α : Type u} (union : α → α → α) : Union α
Union.mk.description: The construction of a union type enables the representation of a type that encompasses all elements generated by a given union operation on pairs of elements from that type.

Inter.mk.code: Inter.mk.{u} {α : Type u} (inter : α → α → α) : Inter α
Inter.mk.description: The intersection operator for a type that combines elements according to a specified binary operation is defined.

SDiff.mk.code: SDiff.mk.{u} {α : Type u} (sdiff : α → α → α) : SDiff α
SDiff.mk.description: A set difference operation can be defined for a type by specifying the properties that determine how to differentiate between two elements.

Exists.elim.code: Exists.elim.{u} {α : Sort u} {p : α → Prop} {b : Prop} (h₁ : ∃ x, p x) (h₂ : ∀ (a : α), p a → b) : b
Exists.elim.description: If there exists an element satisfying a given property, then any conclusion derived from that property can be asserted.

Insert.insert.code: Insert.insert.{u, v} {α : outParam (Type u)} {γ : Type v} [self : Insert α γ] : α → γ → γ
Insert.insert.comment: `insert x xs` inserts the element `x` into the collection `xs`.
Insert.insert.description: An operation is defined that allows an element to be added to a collection of another type.

Quotient.ind.code:
Quotient.ind.{u} {α : Sort u} {s : Setoid α} {motive : Quotient s → Prop} :
  (∀ (a : α), motive ⟦a⟧) → ∀ (q : Quotient s), motive q
Quotient.ind.comment: The analogue of `Quot.ind`: every element of `Quotient s` is of the form `Quotient.mk s a`.
Quotient.ind.description: If a property holds for representatives of a quotient, it holds for all elements of that quotient.

Quotient.inductionOn.code:
Quotient.inductionOn.{u} {α : Sort u} {s : Setoid α} {motive : Quotient s → Prop} (q : Quotient s)
  (h : ∀ (a : α), motive ⟦a⟧) : motive q
Quotient.inductionOn.comment: The analogue of `Quot.inductionOn`: every element of `Quotient s` is of the form `Quotient.mk s a`.
Quotient.inductionOn.description: For any property defined on a quotient type, if that property holds for representatives of each equivalence class, it holds for the entire quotient.

Quotient.exact.code: Quotient.exact.{u} {α : Sort u} {s : Setoid α} {a b : α} : ⟦a⟧ = ⟦b⟧ → a ≈ b
Quotient.exact.description: If two elements belong to the same equivalence class in a quotient, then they are equivalent under the associated relation.

Quotient.lift₂.code:
Quotient.lift₂.{uA, uB, uC} {α : Sort uA} {β : Sort uB} {φ : Sort uC} {s₁ : Setoid α} {s₂ : Setoid β} (f : α → β → φ)
  (c : ∀ (a₁ : α) (b₁ : β) (a₂ : α) (b₂ : β), a₁ ≈ a₂ → b₁ ≈ b₂ → f a₁ b₁ = f a₂ b₂) (q₁ : Quotient s₁)
  (q₂ : Quotient s₂) : φ
Quotient.lift₂.comment: Lift a binary function to a quotient on both arguments.
Quotient.lift₂.fullDefinition: protected abbrev lift₂     (f : α → β → φ)     (c : (a₁ : α) → (b₁ : β) → (a₂ : α) → (b₂ : β) → a₁ ≈ a₂ → b₁ ≈ b₂ → f a₁ b₁ = f a₂ b₂)     (q₁ : Quotient s₁) (q₂ : Quotient s₂)     : φ := by   apply Quotient.lift (fun (a₁ : α) => Quotient.lift (f a₁) (fun (a b : β) => c a₁ a a₁ b (Setoid.refl a₁)) q₂) _ q₁   intros   induction q₂ using Quotient.ind   apply c; assumption; apply Setoid.refl
Quotient.lift₂.description: This definition allows a binary function to be extended to operate on equivalence classes from two quotient types.

PEmpty.elim.code: PEmpty.elim.{u_1, u_2} {C : Sort u_1} : PEmpty.{u_2} → C
PEmpty.elim.comment:
`PEmpty.elim : Empty → C` says that a value of any type can be constructed from
`PEmpty`. This can be thought of as a compiler-checked assertion that a code path is unreachable.

This is a non-dependent variant of `PEmpty.rec`.
PEmpty.elim.fullDefinition: @[macro_inline] def PEmpty.elim {C : Sort _} : PEmpty → C := fun a => nomatch a
PEmpty.elim.description: The elimination of an empty type allows one to derive any type from it, effectively indicating that no values of the empty type exist.

Inter.inter.code: Inter.inter.{u} {α : Type u} [self : Inter α] : α → α → α
Inter.inter.comment: `a ∩ b` is the intersection of`a` and `b`.
Inter.inter.description: The intersection of two sets is a binary operation that produces a new set containing only the elements common to both.

Thunk.get.code: Thunk.get.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (x : Thunk α) : α
Thunk.get.comment:
Forces a thunk to extract the value. This will cache the result,
so a second call to the same function will return the value in O(1)
instead of calling the stored getter function.
Thunk.get.fullDefinition: @[extern "lean_thunk_get_own"] protected def Thunk.get (x : @& Thunk α) : α :=   x.fn ()
Thunk.get.description: Extracting the value from a thunk not only retrieves the stored result but also caches it for efficient future access.

Thunk.pure.code: Thunk.pure.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (a : α) : Thunk α
Thunk.pure.comment: Store a value in a thunk. Note that the value has already been computed, so there is no laziness.
Thunk.pure.fullDefinition: @[extern "lean_thunk_pure"] protected def Thunk.pure (a : α) : Thunk α :=   ⟨fun _ => a⟩
Thunk.pure.description: A thunk is created by storing a pre-computed value, which allows for the encapsulation of the value without introducing laziness.

decidable_of_decidable_of_iff.code: decidable_of_decidable_of_iff {p q : Prop} [Decidable p] (h : p ↔ q) : Decidable q
decidable_of_decidable_of_iff.comment: Transfer a decidability proof across an equivalence of propositions.
decidable_of_decidable_of_iff.fullDefinition: @[inline] def decidable_of_decidable_of_iff [Decidable p] (h : p ↔ q) : Decidable q :=   if hp : p then     isTrue (Iff.mp h hp)   else     isFalse fun hq => absurd (Iff.mpr h hq) hp
decidable_of_decidable_of_iff.description: If one proposition is decidable and is equivalent to another, then the second proposition is also decidable.

imp_self.description: If a proposition is true, then it implies itself and is equivalent to the truth of any statement.

Quotient.liftOn₂.comment: Lift a binary function to a quotient on both arguments.
Quotient.liftOn₂.fullDefinition: protected abbrev liftOn₂     (q₁ : Quotient s₁)     (q₂ : Quotient s₂)     (f : α → β → φ)     (c : (a₁ : α) → (b₁ : β) → (a₂ : α) → (b₂ : β) → a₁ ≈ a₂ → b₁ ≈ b₂ → f a₁ b₁ = f a₂ b₂)     : φ :=   Quotient.lift₂ f c q₁ q₂
Quotient.liftOn₂.description: Applying a binary function to representatives from two separate quotients results in a value in the codomain, ensuring that equivalent inputs yield the same output.

eq_comm.code: eq_comm.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {a b : α} : a = b ↔ b = a
eq_comm.description: The equality relation between two elements is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.

Setoid.trans.code: Setoid.trans.{u} {α : Sort u} [Setoid α] {a b c : α} (hab : a ≈ b) (hbc : b ≈ c) : a ≈ c
Setoid.trans.description: If two elements are related by a relation and the second element is related to a third element, then the first and third elements are also related by the same relation.

Setoid.r.code: Setoid.r.{u} {α : Sort u} [self : Setoid α] : α → α → Prop
Setoid.r.comment: `x ≈ y` is the distinguished equivalence relation of a setoid.
Setoid.r.fullDefinition: r : α → α → Prop   /-- The relation `x ≈ y` is an equivalence relation. -/   iseqv : Equivalence r
Setoid.r.description: The distinguished equivalence relation of a setoid relates two elements in a way that satisfies the properties of equivalence.

Quotient.ind₂.description: A property defined for pairs of equivalence classes can be established if it holds for corresponding representatives from each class.

Quot.inductionOn.code:
Quot.inductionOn.{u} {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} {motive : Quot r → Prop} (q : Quot r)
  (h : ∀ (a : α), motive (Quot.mk r a)) : motive q
Quot.inductionOn.description: The principle allows one to establish a property for equivalence classes by ensuring it holds for representative elements in the class.

Eq.mp.code: Eq.mp.{u} {α β : Sort u} (h : α = β) (a : α) : β
Eq.mp.comment:
If `h : α = β` is a proof of type equality, then `h.mp : α → β` is the induced
"cast" operation, mapping elements of `α` to elements of `β`.

You can prove theorems about the resulting element by induction on `h`, since
`rfl.mp` is definitionally the identity function.
Eq.mp.fullDefinition: @[macro_inline] def Eq.mp {α β : Sort u} (h : α = β) (a : α) : β :=   h ▸ a
Eq.mp.description: A proof of type equality can be used to transform an element of one type into an element of another type that it is equal to, effectively providing a way to "cast" between the two types.

Std.Commutative.mk.code: Std.Commutative.mk.{u} {α : Sort u} {op : α → α → α} (comm : ∀ (a b : α), op a b = op b a) : Std.Commutative op
Std.Commutative.mk.description: A structure is created that encapsulates a binary operation and its property of commutativity, meaning the operation yields the same result regardless of the order of its inputs.

Eq.mpr.code: Eq.mpr.{u} {α β : Sort u} (h : α = β) (b : β) : α
Eq.mpr.comment:
If `h : α = β` is a proof of type equality, then `h.mpr : β → α` is the induced
"cast" operation in the reverse direction, mapping elements of `β` to elements of `α`.

You can prove theorems about the resulting element by induction on `h`, since
`rfl.mpr` is definitionally the identity function.
Eq.mpr.fullDefinition: @[macro_inline] def Eq.mpr {α β : Sort u} (h : α = β) (b : β) : α :=   h ▸ b
Eq.mpr.description: If there is a proof of equality between two types, then this definition provides a way to convert an element of one type to an element of the other type.

Std.Commutative.comm.code: Std.Commutative.comm.{u} {α : Sort u} {op : α → α → α} [self : Std.Commutative op] (a b : α) : op a b = op b a
Std.Commutative.comm.comment: A commutative operation satisfies `a ∘ b = b ∘ a`.
Std.Commutative.comm.description: A commutative operation guarantees that the result of combining two elements is the same regardless of their order.

Equivalence.refl.code: Equivalence.refl.{u} {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} (self : Equivalence r) (x : α) : r x x
Equivalence.refl.comment: An equivalence relation is reflexive: `x ~ x`
Equivalence.refl.description: An equivalence relation satisfies reflexivity, meaning every element is related to itself.

Setoid.iseqv.code: Setoid.iseqv.{u} {α : Sort u} [self : Setoid α] : Equivalence r
Setoid.iseqv.comment: The relation `x ≈ y` is an equivalence relation.
Setoid.iseqv.description: The relation defined by the setoid is confirmed to be an equivalence relation, satisfying reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity.

heq_of_eq.code: heq_of_eq.{u} {α : Sort u} {a a' : α} (h : a = a') : HEq a a'
heq_of_eq.description: The theorem states that if two elements are equal, then they are homotopically equal as well.

Quotient.mk'.code: Quotient.mk'.{u} {α : Sort u} [s : Setoid α] (a : α) : Quotient s
Quotient.mk'.comment:
The canonical quotient map into a `Quotient`.
(This synthesizes the setoid by typeclass inference.)
Quotient.mk'.fullDefinition: protected def mk' {α : Sort u} [s : Setoid α] (a : α) : Quotient s :=   Quotient.mk s a
Quotient.mk'.description: The canonical quotient map creates a quotient type from an element by inferring the associated equivalence relation from the provided typeclass.

HEq.symm.code: HEq.symm.{u} {α β : Sort u} {a : α} {b : β} (h : HEq a b) : HEq b a
HEq.symm.description: If two values are considered quality-equal based on a certain relation, then reversing the comparison will still show that they are quality-equal.

Subsingleton.elim.code: Subsingleton.elim.{u} {α : Sort u} [h : Subsingleton α] (a b : α) : a = b
Subsingleton.elim.description: In a subsingleton type, any two elements are equal, demonstrating the uniqueness of elements in such types.

HasSSubset.mk.code: HasSSubset.mk.{u} {α : Type u} (SSubset : α → α → Prop) : HasSSubset α
HasSSubset.mk.description: The creation of a subtype structure is defined in terms of a binary relation that specifies how elements relate to each other within that structure.

Std.Associative.mk.code:
Std.Associative.mk.{u} {α : Sort u} {op : α → α → α} (assoc : ∀ (a b c : α), op (op a b) c = op a (op b c)) :
  Std.Associative op
Std.Associative.mk.description: A binary operation is defined as associative if the grouping of operations does not affect the result for any three elements.

Std.IdempotentOp.mk.code: Std.IdempotentOp.mk.{u} {α : Sort u} {op : α → α → α} (idempotent : ∀ (x : α), op x x = x) : Std.IdempotentOp op
Std.IdempotentOp.mk.description: An operation is defined as idempotent if applying it to any element with itself yields that same element.

InvImage.code: InvImage.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} (r : β → β → Prop) (f : α → β) : α → α → Prop
InvImage.comment:
The inverse image of `r : β → β → Prop` by a function `α → β` is the relation
`s : α → α → Prop` defined by `s a b = r (f a) (f b)`.
InvImage.fullDefinition: def InvImage {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} (r : β → β → Prop) (f : α → β) : α → α → Prop :=   fun a₁ a₂ => r (f a₁) (f a₂)
InvImage.description: The inverse image of a relation defined on one type can be constructed by applying a function to two elements from another type and using the original relation on their images.

Quotient.recOnSubsingleton.code:
Quotient.recOnSubsingleton.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {s : Setoid α} {motive : Quotient s → Sort v}
  [h : ∀ (a : α), Subsingleton (motive ⟦a⟧)] (q : Quotient s) (f : (a : α) → motive ⟦a⟧) : motive q
Quotient.recOnSubsingleton.fullDefinition: protected abbrev recOnSubsingleton     [h : (a : α) → Subsingleton (motive (Quotient.mk s a))]     (q : Quotient s)     (f : (a : α) → motive (Quotient.mk s a))     : motive q :=   Quot.recOnSubsingleton (h := h) q f
Quotient.recOnSubsingleton.description: This definition provides a method for constructing a result based on a quotient type when all elements of the type have a property that makes them interchangeable.

not_false_iff.description: The statement establishes that the negation of falsehood is logically equivalent to truth.

HasSSubset.SSubset.code: HasSSubset.SSubset.{u} {α : Type u} [self : HasSSubset α] : α → α → Prop
HasSSubset.SSubset.description: A strict subset relation is defined as one set being a proper subset of another.

Std.Associative.assoc.code:
Std.Associative.assoc.{u} {α : Sort u} {op : α → α → α} [self : Std.Associative op] (a b c : α) :
  op (op a b) c = op a (op b c)
Std.Associative.assoc.comment: An associative operation satisfies `(a ∘ b) ∘ c = a ∘ (b ∘ c)`.
Std.Associative.assoc.description: An operation is defined to be associative if it produces the same result when grouping operands in different ways.

Subtype.mk.inj.code:
Subtype.mk.inj.{u} {α : Sort u} {p : α → Prop} {val : α} {property : p val} :
  ∀ {val_1 : α} {property_1 : p val_1}, ⟨val, property⟩ = ⟨val_1, property_1⟩ → val = val_1
Subtype.mk.inj.description: Two elements of a subtype are equal if and only if their underlying values are equal, provided their properties are also satisfied.

PSigma.fst.code: PSigma.fst.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {β : α → Sort v} (self : PSigma β) : α
PSigma.fst.comment: The first component of a dependent pair. If `p : @Sigma α β` then `p.1 : α`.
PSigma.fst.fullDefinition: fst : α   /-- The second component of a dependent pair. If `p : Sigma β` then `p.2 : β p.1`. -/   snd : β fst
PSigma.fst.description: The first component of a dependent pair provides the underlying element from the pair structure.

PSigma.snd.code: PSigma.snd.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {β : α → Sort v} (self : PSigma β) : β self.fst
PSigma.snd.comment: The second component of a dependent pair. If `p : Sigma β` then `p.2 : β p.1`.
PSigma.snd.description: The second component of a dependent pair provides the value associated with the first element of that pair.

true_ne_false.description: The proposition asserts that the statement of truth is not equal to the statement of falsehood.

Setoid.symm.code: Setoid.symm.{u} {α : Sort u} [Setoid α] {a b : α} (hab : a ≈ b) : b ≈ a
Setoid.symm.description: The symmetry property of an equivalence relation asserts that if one element is equivalent to another, then the second element is also equivalent to the first.

Quotient.liftOn.code:
Quotient.liftOn.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} {s : Setoid α} (q : Quotient s) (f : α → β)
  (c : ∀ (a b : α), a ≈ b → f a = f b) : β
Quotient.liftOn.comment:
The analogue of `Quot.liftOn`: if `f : α → β` respects the equivalence relation `≈`,
then it lifts to a function on `Quotient s` such that `lift (mk a) f h = f a`.
Quotient.liftOn.fullDefinition: protected abbrev liftOn {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} {s : Setoid α} (q : Quotient s) (f : α → β) (c : (a b : α) → a ≈ b → f a = f b) : β :=   Quot.liftOn q f c
Quotient.liftOn.description: A function that respects an equivalence relation can be lifted from a set to its quotient, allowing for consistent mapping of elements under the equivalence.

trivial.comment:
`True` is true, and `True.intro` (or more commonly, `trivial`)
is the proof.
trivial.description: The statement confirms that the proposition asserting truth is indeed valid and can be proven simply.

Empty.elim.comment:
`Empty.elim : Empty → C` says that a value of any type can be constructed from
`Empty`. This can be thought of as a compiler-checked assertion that a code path is unreachable.

This is a non-dependent variant of `Empty.rec`.
Empty.elim.fullDefinition: @[macro_inline] def Empty.elim {C : Sort u} : Empty → C := Empty.rec
Empty.elim.description: From a nonexistent value, any type of value can be derived, indicating that such a situation is impossible to reach.

Quotient.hrecOn.code:
Quotient.hrecOn.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {s : Setoid α} {motive : Quotient s → Sort v} (q : Quotient s)
  (f : (a : α) → motive ⟦a⟧) (c : ∀ (a b : α), a ≈ b → HEq (f a) (f b)) : motive q
Quotient.hrecOn.fullDefinition: protected abbrev hrecOn     (q : Quotient s)     (f : (a : α) → motive (Quotient.mk s a))     (c : (a b : α) → (p : a ≈ b) → HEq (f a) (f b))     : motive q :=   Quot.hrecOn q f c end
Quotient.hrecOn.description: This definition describes a method for constructing values in a dependent type from a representative of an equivalence class, along with a way to ensure that these values are equal whenever their representatives are equivalent.

Option.some.injEq.code: Option.some.injEq.{u} {α : Type u} (val : α) : ∀ (val_1 : α), (some val = some val_1) = (val = val_1)
Option.some.injEq.description: If two options containing values are equal, then those values must also be equal.

And.symm.code: And.symm {a b : Prop} : a ∧ b → b ∧ a
And.symm.description: The conjunction of two propositions can be reversed, meaning that if both are true in one order, they are also true in the opposite order.

Quot.recOnSubsingleton.code:
Quot.recOnSubsingleton.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} {motive : Quot r → Sort v}
  [h : ∀ (a : α), Subsingleton (motive (Quot.mk r a))] (q : Quot r) (f : (a : α) → motive (Quot.mk r a)) : motive q
Quot.recOnSubsingleton.comment:
Dependent induction principle for a quotient, when the target type is a `Subsingleton`.
In this case the quotient's side condition is trivial so any function can be lifted.
Quot.recOnSubsingleton.fullDefinition: protected abbrev recOnSubsingleton     [h : (a : α) → Subsingleton (motive (Quot.mk r a))]     (q : Quot r)     (f : (a : α) → motive (Quot.mk r a))     : motive q := by   induction q using Quot.rec   apply f   apply Subsingleton.elim
Quot.recOnSubsingleton.description: This definition describes a dependent induction principle for a quotient type where the target type is a subsingleton, allowing any function to be used for lifting.

Quot.rec.code:
Quot.rec.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} {motive : Quot r → Sort v} (f : (a : α) → motive (Quot.mk r a))
  (h : ∀ (a b : α) (p : r a b), ⋯ ▸ f a = f b) (q : Quot r) : motive q
Quot.rec.comment:
Dependent recursion principle for `Quot`. This constructor can be tricky to use,
so you should consider the simpler versions if they apply:
* `Quot.lift`, for nondependent functions
* `Quot.ind`, for theorems / proofs of propositions about quotients
* `Quot.recOnSubsingleton`, when the target type is a `Subsingleton`
* `Quot.hrecOn`, which uses `HEq (f a) (f b)` instead of a `sound p ▸ f a = f b` assummption
Quot.rec.fullDefinition: protected abbrev rec     (f : (a : α) → motive (Quot.mk r a))     (h : (a b : α) → (p : r a b) → Eq.ndrec (f a) (sound p) = f b)     (q : Quot r) : motive q :=   Eq.ndrecOn (Quot.liftIndepPr1 f h q) ((lift (Quot.indep f) (Quot.indepCoherent f h) q).2)
Quot.rec.description: This definition outlines a dependent recursion principle for quotient types, allowing the construction of functions that depend on the quotient's structure.

Quotient.inductionOn₂.description: For any two equivalence classes, if a property holds for representatives of those classes, then it also holds for the classes themselves.

or_comm.code: or_comm {a b : Prop} : a ∨ b ↔ b ∨ a
or_comm.description: The equivalence between two disjunctions indicates that one proposition is true if and only if the other is, regardless of their order.

imp_true_iff.code: imp_true_iff.{u} (α : Sort u) : α → True ↔ True
imp_true_iff.description: A statement that is true implies that a true condition is equivalent to another true condition.

Sum.casesOn.code:
Sum.casesOn.{u_1, u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {motive : α ⊕ β → Sort u_1} (t : α ⊕ β)
  (inl : (val : α) → motive (Sum.inl val)) (inr : (val : β) → motive (Sum.inr val)) : motive t
Sum.casesOn.fullDefinition: inductive Sum (α : Type u) (β : Type v) where   /-- Left injection into the sum type `α ⊕ β`. If `a : α` then `.inl a : α ⊕ β`. -/   | inl (val : α) : Sum α β   /-- Right injection into the sum type `α ⊕ β`. If `b : β` then `.inr b : α ⊕ β`. -/   | inr (val : β) : Sum α β
Sum.casesOn.description: The construct provides a way to derive a property for a sum type by considering cases for each possible component of the sum.

Quot.hrecOn.code:
Quot.hrecOn.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} {motive : Quot r → Sort v} (q : Quot r)
  (f : (a : α) → motive (Quot.mk r a)) (c : ∀ (a b : α), r a b → HEq (f a) (f b)) : motive q
Quot.hrecOn.comment:
Heterogeneous dependent recursion principle for a quotient.
This may be easier to work with since it uses `HEq` instead of
an `Eq.ndrec` in the hypothesis.
Quot.hrecOn.fullDefinition: protected abbrev hrecOn     (q : Quot r)     (f : (a : α) → motive (Quot.mk r a))     (c : (a b : α) → (p : r a b) → HEq (f a) (f b))     : motive q :=   Quot.recOn q f fun a b p => eq_of_heq <|     have p₁ : HEq (Eq.ndrec (f a) (sound p)) (f a) := eqRec_heq (sound p) (f a)     HEq.trans p₁ (c a b p)
Quot.hrecOn.description: The heterogeneous dependent recursion principle for a quotient allows for defining a function on quotient types using specific values for representatives and ensuring consistency across equivalent representatives through a special equality.

and_comm.code: and_comm {a b : Prop} : a ∧ b ↔ b ∧ a
and_comm.description: The conjunction of two propositions is commutative, meaning that if both are true, the order of their appearance does not affect their truth.

Nat.succ.inj.code: Nat.succ.inj {m n : ℕ} : m.succ = n.succ → m = n
Nat.succ.inj.description: If the successors of two natural numbers are equal, then the original numbers must also be equal.

Not.elim.code: Not.elim.{u_1} {a : Prop} {α : Sort u_1} (H1 : ¬a) (H2 : a) : α
Not.elim.comment:
*Ex falso* for negation: from `¬a` and `a` anything follows. This is the same as `absurd` with
the arguments flipped, but it is in the `Not` namespace so that projection notation can be used.
Not.elim.fullDefinition: def Not.elim {α : Sort _} (H1 : ¬a) (H2 : a) : α := absurd H2 H1
Not.elim.description: From a contradiction derived from both a statement and its negation, it follows that any conclusion can be drawn.

Subtype.mk.injEq.code:
Subtype.mk.injEq.{u} {α : Sort u} {p : α → Prop} (val : α) (property : p val) :
  ∀ (val_1 : α) (property_1 : p val_1), (⟨val, property⟩ = ⟨val_1, property_1⟩) = (val = val_1)
Subtype.mk.injEq.description: Two elements of a subtype are equal if and only if their underlying values are equal, regardless of their properties.

Ne.irrefl.code: Ne.irrefl.{u} {α : Sort u} {a : α} (h : a ≠ a) : False
Ne.irrefl.description: A proposition cannot be both true and false if it states that an element is not equal to itself.

not_true.description: The negation of truth corresponds exactly to falsehood, establishing a logical equivalence between these two concepts.

ne_self_iff_false.code: ne_self_iff_false.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} (a : α) : a ≠ a ↔ False
ne_self_iff_false.description: An element is not equal to itself if and only if a contradiction exists.

cast_heq.code: cast_heq.{u} {α β : Sort u} (h : α = β) (a : α) : HEq (cast h a) a
cast_heq.description: This theorem shows that when an equality between two types is given, the casting of an element from one type to another results in a heterogeneous equality with the original element.

Std.LawfulIdentity.left_id.code:
Std.LawfulIdentity.left_id.{u} {α : Sort u} {op : α → α → α} {o : outParam α} [self : Std.LawfulIdentity op o] (a : α) :
  op o a = a
Std.LawfulIdentity.left_id.description: The left identity element of a binary operation satisfies the property that combining it with any element does not change that element.

Std.LawfulIdentity.right_id.code:
Std.LawfulIdentity.right_id.{u} {α : Sort u} {op : α → α → α} {o : outParam α} [self : Std.LawfulIdentity op o]
  (a : α) : op a o = a
Std.LawfulIdentity.right_id.description: Theorem states that in a structure with a lawful identity, applying the operation with the identity element on any element results in that same element.

Iff.comm.description: The equivalence between two propositions is commutative, meaning that if one proposition implies the other, then the reverse implication also holds.

And.elim.code: And.elim.{u_1} {a b : Prop} {α : Sort u_1} (f : a → b → α) (h : a ∧ b) : α
And.elim.fullDefinition: abbrev And.elim (f : a → b → α) (h : a ∧ b) : α := f h.left h.right
And.elim.description: This definition provides a method for constructing a new value from a conjunction of two propositions by applying a function that takes both propositions as inputs.

Setoid.refl.code: Setoid.refl.{u} {α : Sort u} [Setoid α] (a : α) : a ≈ a
Setoid.refl.description: Every element is related to itself in a setoid structure.

Sum.inl.injEq.code: Sum.inl.injEq.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (val : α) : ∀ (val_1 : α), (inl val = inl val_1) = (val = val_1)
Sum.inl.injEq.description: The equality of two left injections is equivalent to the equality of their respective values.

Sum.inr.injEq.code: Sum.inr.injEq.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (val : β) : ∀ (val_1 : β), (inr val = inr val_1) = (val = val_1)
Sum.inr.injEq.description: The equality of two elements in the right summand of a sum type is equivalent to the equality of the elements themselves.

Prod.mk.injEq.code:
Prod.mk.injEq.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (fst : α) (snd : β) :
  ∀ (fst_1 : α) (snd_1 : β), ((fst, snd) = (fst_1, snd_1)) = (fst = fst_1 ∧ snd = snd_1)
Prod.mk.injEq.description: The equation demonstrating the relationship between the equality of pairs and the equality of their individual components is established.

proof_irrel.code: proof_irrel {a : Prop} (h₁ h₂ : a) : h₁ = h₂
proof_irrel.description: If two proofs lead to the same proposition, then those proofs are indistinguishable.

eq_iff_iff.code: eq_iff_iff {a b : Prop} : a = b ↔ (a ↔ b)
eq_iff_iff.description: The equality of two propositions is equivalent to their logical equivalence.

Quotient.inductionOn₃.description: The theorem facilitates reasoning about elements of quotient types by allowing the application of a motive to representatives of those types, effectively proving properties about the quotients based on their representatives.

Fin.mk.injEq.code:
Fin.mk.injEq {n : ℕ} (val : ℕ) (isLt : val < n) :
  ∀ (val_1 : ℕ) (isLt_1 : val_1 < n), (⟨val, isLt⟩ = ⟨val_1, isLt_1⟩) = (val = val_1)
Fin.mk.injEq.description: If two finite numbers created using the same upper limit are equal as elements, then their underlying values must also be equal.

Quot.recOn.code:
Quot.recOn.{u, v} {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} {motive : Quot r → Sort v} (q : Quot r)
  (f : (a : α) → motive (Quot.mk r a)) (h : ∀ (a b : α) (p : r a b), ⋯ ▸ f a = f b) : motive q
Quot.recOn.comment:
Dependent recursion principle for `Quot`. This constructor can be tricky to use,
so you should consider the simpler versions if they apply:
* `Quot.lift`, for nondependent functions
* `Quot.ind`, for theorems / proofs of propositions about quotients
* `Quot.recOnSubsingleton`, when the target type is a `Subsingleton`
* `Quot.hrecOn`, which uses `HEq (f a) (f b)` instead of a `sound p ▸ f a = f b` assummption
Quot.recOn.fullDefinition: @[inherit_doc Quot.rec] protected abbrev recOn     (q : Quot r)     (f : (a : α) → motive (Quot.mk r a))     (h : (a b : α) → (p : r a b) → Eq.ndrec (f a) (sound p) = f b)     : motive q :=  q.rec f h
Quot.recOn.description: The dependent recursion principle for quotient types allows the construction of functions on quotients by defining their behavior on representatives and ensuring consistent results for equivalent elements.

Nat.succ.injEq.description: The equality of the successors of two natural numbers is equivalent to the equality of the original numbers.

iff_of_true.code: iff_of_true {a b : Prop} (ha : a) (hb : b) : a ↔ b
iff_of_true.description: If one proposition is true and another is also true, then these two propositions are equivalent.

iff_of_false.description: If both propositions are false, then they are logically equivalent.

Equivalence.symm.code: _root_.Equivalence.symm.{u} {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} (self : _root_.Equivalence r) {x y : α} : r x y → r y x
Equivalence.symm.comment: An equivalence relation is symmetric: `x ~ y` implies `y ~ x`
Equivalence.symm.description: An equivalence relation demonstrates symmetry, meaning if one element is related to another, then the second element is also related to the first.

iff_iff_implies_and_implies.code: iff_iff_implies_and_implies (a b : Prop) : (a ↔ b) ↔ (a → b) ∧ (b → a)
iff_iff_implies_and_implies.description: The equivalence of two propositions is true if and only if each implies the other.

Iff.refl.description: Any proposition is logically equivalent to itself.

Sum.inr.inj.code: Sum.inr.inj.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {val : β} : ∀ {val_1 : β}, Sum.inr val = Sum.inr val_1 → val = val_1
Sum.inr.inj.description: If two values are represented as the right component in a sum type, then they are equal if the representations are equal.

ge_iff_le.code: ge_iff_le.{u} {α : Type u} [LE α] {x y : α} : x ≥ y ↔ y ≤ x
ge_iff_le.description: The relation of one element being greater than or equal to another is equivalent to the latter being less than or equal to the former.

Prod.mk.inj.code:
Prod.mk.inj.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {fst : α} {snd : β} :
  ∀ {fst_1 : α} {snd_1 : β}, (fst, snd) = (fst_1, snd_1) → fst = fst_1 ∧ snd = snd_1
Prod.mk.inj.description: The theorem states that if two ordered pairs are equal, then their corresponding components must also be equal.

Function.const_apply.code: Function.const_apply.{u_1, u_2} {β : Sort u_1} {α : Sort u_2} {y : β} {x : α} : Function.const α y x = y
Function.const_apply.description: A constant function evaluated at any input yields the specified constant value.

iff_true_intro.description: If a proposition is true, it is equivalent to the truth itself.

true_imp_iff.description: If a proposition is true, then it is logically equivalent to any other proposition, indicating that the truth of one implies the truth of the other.

Quot.exists_rep.code: Quot.exists_rep.{u} {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} (q : Quot r) : ∃ a, Quot.mk r a = q
Quot.exists_rep.description: For any equivalence class, there exists a representative element such that the equivalence relation applied to that element yields the class.

Sum.recOn.code:
Sum.recOn.{u_1, u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {motive : α ⊕ β → Sort u_1} (t : α ⊕ β)
  (inl : (val : α) → motive (Sum.inl val)) (inr : (val : β) → motive (Sum.inr val)) : motive t
Sum.recOn.fullDefinition: inductive Sum (α : Type u) (β : Type v) where   /-- Left injection into the sum type `α ⊕ β`. If `a : α` then `.inl a : α ⊕ β`. -/   | inl (val : α) : Sum α β   /-- Right injection into the sum type `α ⊕ β`. If `b : β` then `.inr b : α ⊕ β`. -/   | inr (val : β) : Sum α β
Sum.recOn.description: This definition provides a way to construct values in a dependent type from a sum type, based on whether the value comes from the left or right component of the sum.

imp_false.description: A proposition implying a contradiction is equivalent to the negation of that proposition.

instInhabitedProd.code: instInhabitedProd.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [Inhabited α] [Inhabited β] : Inhabited (α × β)
instInhabitedProd.fullDefinition: instance [Inhabited α] [Inhabited β] : Inhabited (α × β) where   default := (default, default)
instInhabitedProd.description: If both components of a product type are inhabited, then the product type itself is also inhabited.

Superset.code: Superset.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [HasSubset α] (a b : α) : Prop
Superset.fullDefinition: abbrev Superset [HasSubset α] (a b : α) := Subset b a
Superset.description: A superset relation indicates that one set contains all elements of another set.

gt_iff_lt.code: gt_iff_lt.{u} {α : Type u} [LT α] {x y : α} : x > y ↔ y < x
gt_iff_lt.description: The relationship between greater than and less than for any two elements states that one element being greater than another is equivalent to the latter being less than the former.

not_not_intro.description: From any proposition that is true, it can be concluded that its negation is false, thereby establishing the principle of double negation introduction.

nonempty_of_exists.code: nonempty_of_exists.{u} {α : Sort u} {p : α → Prop} : (∃ x, p x) → Nonempty α
nonempty_of_exists.description: The theorem states that if there exists at least one element satisfying a property, then the type contains at least one element.

cast_eq.code: cast_eq.{u} {α : Sort u} (h : α = α) (a : α) : cast h a = a
cast_eq.description: This theorem asserts that when an element is cast using an equality that relates it to itself, the result is equal to the original element.

le_of_eq_of_le.code: le_of_eq_of_le.{u} {α : Type u} {a b c : α} [LE α] (h₁ : a = b) (h₂ : b ≤ c) : a ≤ c
le_of_eq_of_le.description: If two elements are equal and the second element is less than or equal to a third element, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third element.

Subsingleton.helim.code: Subsingleton.helim.{u} {α β : Sort u} [h₁ : Subsingleton α] (h₂ : α = β) (a : α) (b : β) : HEq a b
Subsingleton.helim.description: If two types are equal and one is a singleton, then any element from the singleton type is equal to any element from the other type.

Eq.to_iff.code: Eq.to_iff {a b : Prop} : a = b → (a ↔ b)
Eq.to_iff.description: If two propositions are equal, then they are logically equivalent.

Thunk.mk.code: Thunk.mk.{u} {α : Type u} (fn : Unit → α) : Thunk α
Thunk.mk.comment:
Constructs a new thunk from a function `Unit → α`
that will be called when the thunk is forced.
Thunk.mk.description: A thunk is created from a function that takes a unit input and produces a value, to be evaluated only when needed.

DoResultPR.pure.code: DoResultPR.pure.{u} {α β σ : Type u} : α → σ → DoResultPR α β σ
DoResultPR.pure.comment: `pure (a : α) s` means that the block exited normally with return value `a`
DoResultPR.pure.description: The pure function represents a successful execution of a computation that returns a specified value along with a given state.

DoResultPR.return.code: DoResultPR.return.{u} {α β σ : Type u} : β → σ → DoResultPR α β σ
DoResultPR.return.comment: `return (b : β) s` means that the block exited via a `return b` early-exit command
DoResultPR.return.description: The early-exit command in a computation returns a specified value along with a state, encapsulating the result in a particular context.

Std.IdempotentOp.idempotent.code: Std.IdempotentOp.idempotent.{u} {α : Sort u} {op : α → α → α} [self : Std.IdempotentOp op] (x : α) : op x x = x
Std.IdempotentOp.idempotent.comment: An idempotent operation satisfies `a ∘ a = a`.
Std.IdempotentOp.idempotent.description: An idempotent operation applied to the same element yields that element itself.

ForIn.mk.code:
ForIn.mk.{u, v, u₁, u₂} {m : Type u₁ → Type u₂} {ρ : Type u} {α : outParam (Type v)}
  (forIn : {β : Type u₁} → [inst : Monad m] → ρ → β → (α → β → m (ForInStep β)) → m β) : ForIn m ρ α
ForIn.mk.description: A structure for defining a monadic iteration process over a type is created, parameterized by specific types and a function that describes the iteration steps.

ForInStep.done.code: ForInStep.done.{u} {α : Type u} : α → ForInStep α
ForInStep.done.comment:
`.done a` means that we should early-exit the loop.
`.done` is produced by calls to `break` or `return` in the loop.
ForInStep.done.description: The concept describes a mechanism indicating an early exit from a loop using a specific condition.

ForInStep.yield.code: ForInStep.yield.{u} {α : Type u} : α → ForInStep α
ForInStep.yield.comment:
`.yield a` means that we should continue the loop.
`.yield` is produced by `continue` and reaching the bottom of the loop body.
ForInStep.yield.description: This theorem describes a mechanism for continuing a loop by producing a step that yields a specific element, allowing the loop to proceed with that element.
